Main.dc.html.title: The look · ink, paper, one red ribbon

Flow.dc.html.title: Fold continuity · what happens when you open and close

t-closed.text: Closed · 5.4″ outer display · 466 × 678 pt · one hand, one thumb

t-open.text: Open flat · 7.6″ inner display · 951 × 669 pt · the fold is the spine of a book

t-poses.text: Half-folded poses · the hinge holds 15°–165° · content away from the crease, controls where the hand is

t-flow.text: Continuity · nothing restarts when the phone changes shape

s-crease.text: The crease is read at runtime with reservedRegions(kind: .division). Text columns keep an inner margin of division width + 24 pt. No tap target ever sits on the fold. In book pose the gutter widens and a soft page shadow appears, so the crease reads as a feature, not a flaw.

s-vertical.text: Open wide, the control rail sits on the right edge under the thumb (Apple's vertical toolbar, as Things 3 does). The two tab words on the closed phone, Said and Read, become the two page headings when the phone opens.

s-ribbon.text: The ribbon tab at the top of the closed phone is the whole 'now playing' UI. It is a ribbon hanging out of a shut book: tap it to pick up where you left off. When nothing is in progress it is simply not there.

s-lectern.text: Laptop pose uses ArrangementView in split style with the division horizontal: the top view is the transcript (or the book text), the bottom view is the transport. Type steps up to 23 pt so a person across a table can follow. The same layout serves reading aloud while cooking: text on top, big transport below.

s-night.text: Tent pose: the device reports a reserved division, and only one half faces the reader. Verso shows this StandBy-style view: near-black paper, ember red, the chapter and a sleep timer. Tapping either half pauses, so there is no need to find a button in the dark.

s-note.text: Margin notes are the point where recorder and reader meet. Hold the corner, speak, let go. The note is transcribed on-device and pinned to the sentence Ava was reading, with word timestamps on both sides. Later, 'Read my notes back' plays your notes in your Personal Voice, in book order.
